chapter: On the road with the Moores
title: Dancing the Bugle Call Rag for Sissle and Blake
summary: Green asks Noble Sissle's band to play Bugle Call Rag fast and dances with handsprings and a wheel step while Brown Skin Buddies performers and Tom Bailey watch.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And then -- so Mr. Sissle asked me, says, 'What can I do for you? What would you like?'
I don't think -- let's just go back a little bit, Chuck, because I -- explain who was there -- because I don't think it's been recorded yet, who was there watching you dancing.

Oh, that was Mr. Shelton Brooks. He was the composer of 'Some of These Days,' 'Darktown Strutter's Ball' and some other songs, and I think he liked me because I sang his song, 'Darktown Strutter's Ball,' you see, and my aunt had taught me a little step to do, you know, like to go off. See, that was the last song I sang, and that's probably what put the idea into the audience's mind that I could dance.

Well, there was Sissle and Blake, as I'm saying, and at that time there was Chinch and Ellerby's More Show. They had a show called Brown Skin Buddies. And they was finishing up their tour. The was finishing entirely

with traveling, I mean you know doing the show throughout the South, and, you know, they was happening having to be standing in the wings watching, you know, especially when someone would stop the show or something, see. And they were looking for talent, I guess.

So -- so much for that. They were about the most important people there, and, of course, Mr. Tom Bailey, he was always proud of his -- if somebody, a new talent, they'd get a break or something, was discovered in his theater, see. So I went out onstage like I said, like Mr. Brooks, Shelton Brooks told me to, and I asked Mr. Sissel Le did they know the "Bugle Call Rag," and he smiled and laughed at his band, you know, and his musicians and said, "Do we know Bugle Call Rag."
And then he asked me, says, "How fast would you like it." So I say, "Well, as fast as you can, you know.

So he smiled, and he struck up the band. So they started to playing the "Bugle call Rag," and, see, I was thinking about my mother sitting in the audience, you see, Georgella Green, and, oh, I did everything. I did,everything that come in my mind, I tried to do, you see, which, luckily, with God's help, I was able to carry it off, you see. The people enjoyed it, you see.
And I got big applause, large applause. They just
What kind of things did you do?

Oh, man, I did -- well, first I did -- I did the handspring. That's to start it off, you know, because I knowed a little -- my playmates liked that, you see. And -- but I was doing it to the music. And then I'd land on my feet. I'd start back to dancing, you know, and I got some kind of step I could do. I'd call it the wheel, you see, and I was going around and around and around and around, get a hand, get applause and so forth.

And I just danced and danced and danced. Then I finished, you know, and took a bow. Bow -- when I see people -- I'd see shows where people, they would turn around and bow over to the audience, and that was the finish of a dance. So that's what I did. And I ran off the stage, you see, I come back, and I bowed about three times. So I'd learned how to bow now, you know. I guess you call that becoming a ham.
